text:
anna: Quick heads-up — ran into a weird customer report: app sees 429s only for some model families (e.g., rdx-xxl) but not others, even though overall org usage < org quota. Seems burst caps per-model are being enforced but the response is opaque.
kevin: Yeah we've had per-model burst tokens in the runtime for a while. Currently we just emit 429 + Retry-After. No headers about which quota hit or available burst left.
maria: That makes it hard for product to show helpful fallback UX. Customers just see 'rate limited' and retry blindly. Can we expose which quota (org/key/model) and remaining burst in headers?
tim: From a UX POV we should return machine-friendly hints so client can fallback smoothly: suggested_fallbacks and estimated_costs. Example header idea: `X-Quota-Hit: model:rdx-xxl`, `X-Burst-Remaining: 0`, `X-Retry-After: 30` and a JSON body with suggested lower-cost model ids.
kevin: Implementation notes: the runtime tracks three buckets: org, key, model-family. First one to exhaust wins. We can plumb the winner into the response. Low-risk change. Need to watch PII/security in headers.
anna: Also we need telemetry: count of 429s by cause (org/key/model) and histogram of time-until-replenish so we can tune burst sizes. Ops wants to be able to query "429s caused by model-family quota" in Kibana.
ops-bot: noted — adding a new metric 'quota.429.cause' with tag 'cause:model_family|org|key' and tag 'model_family' when applicable.
maria: For the Console, we'll show a little banner: "Requests to rdx-xxl currently rate-limited; suggest rdx-large or rdx-medium" and a CTA to change route model. The API needs to provide `suggested_fallbacks` as a list.
kevin: Design for response payload example: ```json
{
  "error": "rate_limited",
  "cause": "model_family",
  "model": "rdx-xxl",
  "retry_after": 30,
  "suggested_fallbacks": ["rdx-large","rdx-medium"],
  "headers": {
    "X-Quota-Hit": "model:rdx-xxl",
    "X-Burst-Remaining": "0"
  }
}
```
anna: Edge cases: what if fallback models are incompatible (different tokenization or missing features)? We should only suggest compatible families and include a confidence flag.
tim: UI needs the confidence flag and an estimated delta in latency/cost if we surface it. We can show "~3x cheaper" or "~2x faster" for clarity.
kevin: I'll spike the header addition + telemetry and a small API body change. Plan: 1) runtime emits quota cause and remaining burst in response; 2) router surfaces suggested fallbacks computed from model graph; 3) metrics recorded. I'll open an RFC for the header names and payload.
maria: Awesome — can you add a short backwards-compatible flag so Console can opt-in? We should avoid breaking SDKs that parse 429 bodies.
kevin: Will do. ETA: spike by EOD Friday, RFC early next week.
anna: Great — thanks. Follow-up: please include example of the HTTP response (headers + body) in the RFC and a short migration note for SDKs.
ops-bot: action: kevin -> create spike branch and RFC. action: maria -> prototype Console banner using mock API.
kevin: ack.
